A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoPT and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite the relocation of radiosity experiments and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original pre-training and fine-tuning experiments across five industrial simulation benchmarks, plus Cornell-box radiosity results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds broader geometry pre-training, transient DTCHull prediction, additional backbone evaluations, and repeated-run statistics.

M1.justification: The synthetic particle dynamics, trajectory supervision, pre-training and fine-tuning objectives, and Algorithm 1 are retained. V2 evaluates the existing framework on additional backbones and a transient task without specifying a new algorithmic component or objective.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 expands pre-training beyond cars, airplanes, and watercraft to all 55 ShapeNet categories and over 250,000 generated HY3D-Bench geometries. Appendix F adds current-to-next-field transient DTCHull prediction. Radiosity was already evaluated in v1 and is relocated rather than newly added.

E2.justification: The geometry-only baselines and comparisons with Transolver, Transolver++, Galerkin Transformer, GNOT, UPT, GAOT, and GINO are retained. Galerkin and GNOT already appear in v1's Figure 8; v2's Table 4 adds GeoPT-pretrained versions of these backbones rather than new comparison methods.

E3.justification: V2 adds a three-corpus GeoPT-Huge comparison and pretrained-versus-scratch evaluations on additional backbones. The new transient experiment predicts the next field from the current observation and uses a velocity norm one-fifth of the steady-state value. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and Table 3 training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 10 extends the geometry-diversity analysis to general and generated shapes, while Table 4(b) tests whether pre-training benefits depend on the Transolver backbone. Existing geometry-feature, trajectory-step, velocity-sensitivity, convergence, and worst-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. V2's Table 7 reports standard deviations over five runs across all five industrial benchmarks and several training-data fractions. The accompanying text introduces 95% confidence intervals and an equivalence margin of 0.001, although interval bounds and test details are absent. This establishes newly reported statistics, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial result blocks for broader pre-training and transfer. Table 4 reports transient DTCHull relative L2 of 0.05402 versus 0.06189 from scratch, plus pretrained Galerkin and GNOT results across five benchmarks. Figure 10 reports gains from broader geometry corpora. Existing benchmark tables and radiosity MAEs of 0.090 versus 0.097 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Remark 4.2 and Equation (8) relate optimal zero-loss native and lifted predictors through velocity averaging and slicing at t=0. This adds a limited formal relationship; the existing transport-equation interpretation and mass-conservation proposition move from Appendix B to A without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: geometry-derived dynamics-aware pre-training, broad physics transfer, 20–60% reductions in labeled-data requirements, faster convergence, and favorable scaling. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Remark 4.2 adds an expectation-based explanation of information loss in native pre-training. Appendix F motivates smaller transient velocity prompts through shorter-term correlations, and Section 5.3 interprets general-shape pre-training as supporting foundation-model development. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F supplies the transient-specific fine-tuning prescription of reducing the velocity norm fivefold. Existing data-generation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware, runtime information, and code-access information are retained. Implementation details for the newly expanded pre-training corpora remain brief.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning foundation models, HY3D-Bench, Hunyuan3D 2.5, and Transolver-3, supporting limited additional positioning around general-purpose physics models. The related-work argument remains largely unchanged; several other reference edits update publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 introduces Section 5.3, integrates the former radiosity appendix into the main discussion and implementation appendix, and reorders implementation subsections. It also adds acknowledgements and updates publication and contact text. Most existing prose and the overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the geometry-scaling plot and examples in Figure 10 and new Tables 4 and 7. Radiosity Figure 9 moves into the main text with a revised caption, while existing figures and tables are reflowed, resized, and renumbered. The established visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: The broader geometry experiment and transient/backbone tests strengthen previously limited evidence for GeoPT's generality, while five-run standard deviations make its data-efficiency results more assessable. Existing results are preserved. The improvement is limited by sparse specifications for the new experiments and the absence of interval bounds or detailed procedures supporting the confidence-interval claim.
